headline: All majors below the 200-day line, momentum flat to diverging, but whales are moving bitcoin off exchanges while funding stays expensive.
paragraphs: The regime is underwater across the board. Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, XRP, BNB, Dogecoin, and Cardano are all trading below their 200-day simple moving averages, and not one of them has a golden cross to suggest a near-term pivot. Bitcoin sits at 63,653, down 0.34 percent on the day and 49 percent off its 12-month high of 124,773. Ethereum is worse: 1,904 on a 0.78 percent decline and 60.6 percent below its 12-month peak. Solana has fallen 70.4 percent from 247.56 to 73.25 over the year. This is a bear regime, period. The only noise is that Bitcoin's 7-day and 30-day returns are flat to slightly negative (down 1.59 and 2.97 percent respectively), while Ethereum has printed a small 7-day gain of 1.81 percent and a 30-day rise of 6.36 percent. That is the sort of relative strength that earns no celebration in a market where every major asset sits below its 200-day anchor.

Momentum is weak and diverging. Bitcoin's RSI-14 sits at 47.4, a midpoint reading that hints at neither overbought nor oversold condition, and its MACD is below its signal line, confirming the downtrend. Ethereum is worse off: RSI at 56.3 sounds neutral on the surface, but the MACD is also below signal, which means the upside energy of the last seven days is not supported by trend momentum. Solana's RSI of 42.7 and XRP's 42.9 are both in the lower half, again with MACD below signal across the board except for BNB and Dogecoin, where MACD has crossed above signal. That is a small tell, not a reversal. In a market where all seven majors remain below the 200-day line and the crowd is in fear (gauge at 31, a 22-to-33 range over the last 30 days), a MACD cross in two altcoins does not rewire the frame.

Positioning is expensive relative to the crowd's nervousness. Bitcoin funding on OKX is at 0.96 basis points per 8 hours, which annualizes to 10.5 percent; Ethereum's 0.34 basis points annualizes to 3.8 percent. These are not fire-sale rates. Bitcoin's open interest sits at 2.09 billion dollars, and the long-to-short ratio is 1.14, meaning longs outnumber shorts but not by a wide margin. Ethereum's ratio is stronger at 1.33, Solana's at 2.01, but Dogecoin and XRP have ratios of 4.99 and 3.61 respectively, suggesting an extreme crowding of longs in smaller positions. Over the last 22 to 24 hours, liquidations have favored shorts: Bitcoin saw 636,650 dollars of shorts liquidated against 140,635 of longs, and Ethereum saw 2.69 million in shorts against 182,476 in longs. Solana and XRP follow the same pattern. This is a signal that leveraged short holders are getting shaken out, but it sits atop a market where longs in the altcoins are disproportionately positioned for their market caps.

Whale flows are the tensest signal in the tape. Over the last 48 hours, Bitcoin has seen a net outflow of 103 million dollars, the whole print driven by Bitcoin leaving exchanges: 168 million out versus 65 million in. The two largest single moves are both from Kraken: 117.98 million and 50.07 million moving into cold wallets. This is accumulation behavior, the classic sign of conviction holders locking coins away during a downturn. The contradiction is the weekly history: the last four weekly nets show minus 86.7 million, plus 385.7 million, plus 1.075 billion, and plus 67.2 million. Two weeks ago, the net was enormously positive (1.075 billion to exchanges), then it reversed sharply. That flip from inflow to outflow, sustained over the last two weekly periods, is a real tension. Stablecoin float stands at 306.24 billion, down 1.02 percent over the month, so dry powder is not accumulating. The whales are buying spot, not the broader crowd.

Spot ETF flows into Bitcoin and Ethereum are steady and positive. Bitcoin saw 101.7 million dollars in on August 7th, with all five of the last five sessions in the same direction and a 865.3 million five-session net. Ethereum printed 49.6 million on the same date, with four of the last five days in the same direction and a 243.7 million five-session cumulative. This is the traditional-finance bid refusing to leave the table despite the fear gauge at 31 and every major asset below its 200-day line. That is the other half of the tension: institutions are buying while whales are moving spot to cold storage and the derivatives market is either funding longs expensively or liquidating them on the margins.

Watch three things: first, whether the MACD crosses in BNB and Dogecoin mature into a broader momentum shift or die in the drawdown; second, whether Bitcoin closes another session above 63,500 or rolls back further, as the 200-day line is not a support anymore, it is a resistance; and third, whether the whale accumulation pattern (off-exchange net outflow over the last two weeks) persists, because if it does and the stablecoin float begins to rise again, that is a frame change in its infancy. For now, the tape shows a bear regime with expensive leverage, institutional bid, and whale accumulation all in the same frame, which is the definition of a market in early capitulation before a recovery attempt, not proof of one.
